blocks.text: Breaking Down the Real Price Delta: WELL Hygiene vs. Legacy Cleaning

During commercial janitorial RFP evaluations, procurement committees frequently assume that upgrading from a legacy cleaning specification to an IWBI WELL Building Standard v2 hygiene protocol will inflate the annual facility budget by 20% to 30%. That misconception stems from vendors who mark up green chemical line items while still calculating consumption based on wasteful free-pour legacy habits.

When analyzed at the unit-cost level across labor, chemical concentrates, equipment depreciation, and restroom consumables, the true net variance between a legacy commercial contract and a WELL-aligned contract is surprisingly narrow. Because direct janitorial labor ($35 to $65 per hour for standard crews; $55 to $95 per hour for specialty technicians) represents 70% to 78% of every commercial cleaning invoice, a 10% shift in chemical concentrate cost moves the total monthly invoice by less than 1%. The real cost delta lies in high-touch disinfection dwell-time labor, microfiber laundering logistics, and touchless restroom consumable specifications.

blocks.text: Chemical Supply Economics: Free-Pour Legacy vs. Closed-Loop Eco Concentrates

A gallon of legacy commercial multi-surface cleaner or quaternary disinfectant often carries a lower wholesale sticker price per jug than a third-party certified Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice concentrate. However, legacy janitorial closets without closed-loop wall proportioners suffer from an industry-wide 30% to 45% over-pouring rate—commonly called the 'glug-glug method'—where night-shift staff pour unmeasured chemical straight into mop buckets.

Over-concentrated legacy solutions leave a tacky surfactant film on VCT and LVT vinyl floors (1.04 flooring multiplier) and ceramic tile grout (1.12 flooring multiplier). That sticky residue attracts shoe soil twice as fast, forcing more frequent scrubbing and creating slip hazards when damp. Under a WELL building hygiene protocol, closed-loop dilution locks chemical dispensing at exact 1:64, 1:128, or 1:256 ratios. In practice, a facility spending $180 per month on free-poured conventional cleaners frequently drops its net chemical spend to $145 per month after switching to metered WELL-compliant concentrates.

blocks.title: Eliminate C-Fold Paper Towel Waste Under WELL Feature W08
blocks.text: Legacy office restrooms stocked with multifold or C-fold paper towels experience 25% to 35% sheet clumping—where damp hands pull out three or four folded sheets at once and drop half into the trash. Switching to sensor-activated or mechanical touchless high-capacity roll towel dispensers under WELL Feature W08 (Hygiene Support) cuts paper tonnage by up to 22% while eliminating shared dispenser touchpoints.
Consumables Comparison: Touchless Roll Towels, Tissue, and High-Density Liners

These 16-micron high-density polyethylene (HDPE) liners use a reinforced star-seal bottom that conforms to 44-gallon round Brute barrels, preventing liquid leaks while reducing raw plastic resin weight per case.

blocks.text: Labor Productivity and Equipment Depreciation Differences
Why does direct labor cost 8% to 10% more in a WELL building hygiene program if consumable costs drop? The labor delta comes down to three verifiable nightly duties that legacy crews routinely skip:

items.name: Verified High-Touch Wet Contact Dwell Time
items.text: Legacy crews spray and immediately wipe door pulls, conference table power pods, and faucet handles. WELL-trained crews pre-clean visible soil, apply EPA-registered low-toxicity disinfectant, and allow full label contact time before drying, adding roughly 12 to 18 minutes per 10,000 square feet.

items.name: Microfiber Pad Change-Outs Between Rooms
items.text: Instead of pushing one 24-ounce cotton string mop across four restrooms and an elevator lobby, technicians swap color-coded flat microfiber pads after each restroom zone and bag soiled pads for hot-water laundering.

items.name: Audit Log Completion and IAQ Equipment Checks
items.text: Night supervisors spend 10 minutes at shift close logging chemical dilution batch numbers, checking HEPA vacuum bag fill levels, and signing digital QR zone checklists required for annual WELL v2 recertification.

blocks.text: When the WELL Protocol Pays for Itself: Asset Preservation & Absenteeism

Evaluating the $403 monthly delta on a 15,000-square-foot Class A office ($4,836 per year, or just $0.32 per square foot annually) requires looking at facility capital preservation. High-alkaline legacy cleaners and aggressive rotary brush scrubbing strip factory wear layers off LVT and degrade carpet tile backing adhesives 30% faster than neutral-pH low-moisture maintenance. Extending a 15,000-square-foot commercial carpet installation ($65,000+ replacement capital cost) by even two years saves over $6,500 annually in amortized capital expenditure—more than offsetting the entire janitorial compliance premium.

faqs.q: Why are consumables in our WELL hygiene quote priced lower per square foot than our old legacy contract?
faqs.a: Legacy contracts frequently bundle low-capacity C-fold paper towels and un-metered bulk soaps that suffer from high pilferage, clumping waste, and frequent restocking trips. Switching to 800-foot high-capacity touchless roll towel systems and 16-micron star-seal high-density liners under a WELL specification typically drives consumable costs toward the $0.014–$0.016/sq ft/visit midpoint rather than the $0.022–$0.025 top end.

faqs.q: Does switching from 5x/week to 3x/week hybrid cleaning change the WELL vs. conventional cost delta?
faqs.a: On a 3x-week schedule (13.0 visits per month at a 0.95 frequency multiplier, compared to 21.65 visits at a 0.90 multiplier for 5x-week), total monthly labor drops by roughly 36% for both conventional and WELL programs. However, the percentage delta between legacy and WELL remains steady at 6% to 10% because high-touch disinfection dwell times and HEPA filtration standards apply on every visit.

faqs.q: Can our janitorial vendor charge specialty hourly rates ($55–$95/hr) for standard nightly WELL cleaning?
faqs.a: No. Nightly vacuuming, trash pulling, restroom sanitation, and damp mopping under a WELL SOP should still be billed within standard commercial janitorial hourly benchmarks ($35 to $65 per hour, adjusted for your local metro multiplier). Specialty rates ($55 to $95/hr) should only apply to periodic technical work such as quarterly floor stripping, electrostatic bio-decontamination, or certified IAQ testing.

faqs.q: What contract exclusions should we watch for when comparing legacy and WELL cleaning bids?
faqs.a: Verify whether bidders exclude microfiber laundry equipment, wall-mounted chemical dilution hardware, interior glass partitions ($15–$35/visit), and HEPA vacuum replacement bags from their base per-square-foot price. Require an all-inclusive per-visit rate so lowball conventional bidders cannot add back hidden equipment surcharges after contract award.
